newsitem.title: USA: Tornadoes hit Massachusetts and New Hampshire.
newsitem.headline: Tornadoes hit Massachusetts and New Hampshire.

text.p: Tornadoes and heavy thunderstorms caused widespread damage Thursday in western Massachusetts and southern New Hampshire, officials said.
No deaths were reported but the storms knocked trees into houses and blocked roads, causing some minor injuries, said Massachusetts Emergency Management Agency director Peter LaPorte.
LaPorte told Reuters said the agency's Framingham headquarters was struck by lightening. "It scared the heck out of us," he said.
Officials believe up to eight small tornadoes touched down in western Massachusetts. Damage was reported in the towns of Great Barrington, Monterey, Otis, Heath, Charlemont, Richmond and Florida.
"We were very lucky that we did not have more damage," LaPorte said. "There's a lot of tree damage and scattered power outages ... but we're not seeing any loss of life at this point."

Tornadoes also knocked down trees and collapsed several buildings in the New Hampshire towns of Greenfield and Swanzey, but no major injuries were reported, according to the Cheshire County Sheriff's Department.
